Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

could you shape these notes into a draft update for the alder quay striders email, for members and people who come along to the open runs, not a press release and not a race report. keep it friendly and useful, and don't make it sound like the club has a big budget or a staffed office. the notes are all the material to work from. the club uses the name alder quay striders, usually shortened to AQS after the full name has appeared once. we're based around the north quay in Bellwick; the boathouse steps are where people meet, not a club building. we have no paid coaches in these notes, so don't call anyone a coach. the regular organizers are volunteers.

this is an update for the first half of may. the first saturday social run is may 4, the second is may 18. both meet at 9:00 am at the boathouse steps. people can choose either the shorter loop, about 3 kilometres, or the longer one, about 6 kilometres. the routes share the first stretch along the riverside path and split at the old signal post. the short group turns back there; the longer group follows the path to the footbridge and returns on the east bank. don't describe either as a race or promise that everyone will finish at the same time. on may 4, the riverside path has a temporary diversion by the net sheds, and runners need to follow the signed path around the works. the diversion is only for that saturday as far as the notes say. for may 18, there isn't a route change listed.

we also have a midweek easy run on tuesdays, leaving at 6:15 pm from the same steps. usual distance is roughly 4 kilometres, though people sometimes stop earlier if they need to. it is an easy conversational pace and nobody has to keep up with the quickest person. one of the regulars, imani, said, “i like that we can talk the whole way and still call it a run.” we need to make it clear this is a group run, not individual coaching or a guaranteed training plan. if heavy rain or a safety issue means a run has to change, organizers will post an update in the club's public notice channel by 5:30 pm that day. no cancellation is currently listed. please don't turn that into a claim that weather will be clear.

membership is optional for the open runs. new people can come to one of those sessions without signing up first, but should arrive ten minutes early so a volunteer can explain the route and ask what distance they want. the group doesn't have a bag drop or changing rooms. water is available from the public tap beside the boathouse steps, but people should bring a bottle if they want water during the run. the nearest public toilets are in the market hall, about a five-minute walk away, and the hall opens at 8:30 am on saturday. don't imply that the club controls the tap or the toilets. a runner called jo said, “i was nervous about turning up on my own, but someone waited with me while i got my bearings.” use that as a normal quote and keep jo's name lowercase as supplied.

there are a few practical notes for the email too. dogs aren't part of the group runs, because the paths are narrow where the two groups meet. people may bring children who can comfortably manage their chosen distance, but anyone under 16 needs to stay with their accompanying adult. the run uses public paths, so remind people to be considerate of walkers and cyclists and to leave room at the bridge. don't describe the route as closed to other users. we don't have a formal pace chart. for anyone unsure which group to pick, say they can tell the volunteer at the start and choose the shorter loop; don't say they can switch halfway unless the notes say that, which they don't. there are no entry fees for these open sessions.

for a small numbered section in the draft, please include the three first-visit reminders below, in this order, without turning them into a long rules list:
1) arrive ten minutes early
2) choose about 3 km or about 6 km
3) check the notice channel for a same-day change

another volunteer, martin, put it this way: “we're not trying to make every run an event; we just want it to be easy to join in.” it can appear near the end, but don't present martin as the club's official spokesperson. i also have a note from the route check: the old signal post is visible from the riverside path but the footbridge sign is partly hidden by a tree. mention that only if it fits naturally and doesn't make the directions confusing. nobody has confirmed when the tree will be trimmed. the east-bank return has a paved section and then a short gravel stretch, which can be uneven after rain. we have no accessibility audit or step-free route information, so don't claim that either loop is accessible for everyone.

don't add contact details, a website, a registration link, membership prices, a club history, or a sign-off from a named officer; none are in the notes. no invented attendance numbers or claims about how many new members joined. keep the May 4 diversion attached to that date and retain the conditional wording about a possible change if heavy rain or a safety issue arises. use the quotes as quotes, not as claims about everybody's experience. please make it readable as an email draft, with a short heading and a brief opening, the schedule and practical details, the numbered first-visit section, and a modest closing. no need to explain these instructions back to me.", "output": "Please draft a friendly, useful email update for members and people who attend Alder Quay Striders’ open runs. This is an update for the first half of May, not a press release or race report. Use only the information below. Keep the tone welcoming and modest; do not imply that the club has a large budget or staffed office. Refer to the club first as Alder Quay Striders, then as AQS. The club is based around the north quay in Bellwick. The boathouse steps are the meeting point, not a club building. Organizers are volunteers, and there are no paid coaches mentioned.

Include a short heading, brief opening, schedule and practical details, a numbered first-visit section, and a modest closing. Use the supplied quotations as ordinary attributed quotes. Do not invent contact details, a website, registration link, prices, club history, named-officer sign-off, attendance figures, membership growth, or other facts.

**Schedule**
- The first Saturday social run is May 4; the second is May 18. Both start at 9:00 am at the boathouse steps. Runners may choose an approximately 3 km short loop or an approximately 6 km long loop. Both follow the riverside path at first and split at the old signal post. The short group turns back there; the long group continues to the footbridge and returns on the east bank. Do not call these races or promise that everyone will finish together.
- On May 4 only, the riverside path has a temporary diversion by the net sheds. Runners should follow the signed path around the works. No route change is listed for May 18.
- There is also a Tuesday easy run, leaving the boathouse steps at 6:15 pm. It is usually about 4 km, and people sometimes stop earlier if needed. Describe it as an easy, conversational group run—not individual coaching or a guaranteed training plan. Imani said, “i like that we can talk the whole way and still call it a run.”

If heavy rain or a safety issue means a run has to change, organizers will post an update in the club’s public notice channel by 5:30 pm that day. No cancellation is currently listed. Keep this conditional; do not suggest that clear weather is guaranteed.

**Joining and practical details**
Membership is optional for open runs. New people may attend an open session without signing up first and should arrive ten minutes early so a volunteer can explain the route and ask which distance they want. There is no bag drop or changing room. A public tap is beside the boathouse steps; people should bring a bottle if they want water during the run. Public toilets are in the market hall, about a five-minute walk away. The hall opens at 8:30 am on Saturday. Do not imply the club controls the tap or toilets.

Jo said, “i was nervous about turning up on my own, but someone waited with me while i got my bearings.” Keep Jo’s name lowercase as supplied. Dogs are not part of the group runs because the paths are narrow where the groups meet. Children who can comfortably manage their chosen distance may come, but anyone under 16 must stay with their accompanying adult. Remind runners to be considerate of walkers and cyclists on the public paths and to leave room at the bridge; do not suggest the paths are closed to others. There is no formal pace chart. Anyone unsure which group to choose can tell the volunteer at the start and choose the shorter loop. Do not say runners can switch halfway. Open sessions have no entry fee.

The east-bank return includes a paved section and a short gravel stretch that can be uneven after rain. The old signal post is visible from the riverside path, but the footbridge sign is partly hidden by a tree. Include that detail only if it fits naturally and does not make the directions confusing. There is no confirmed timing for trimming the tree. The club has no accessibility audit or step-free route information, so do not claim either loop is accessible for everyone.

**First-visit reminders**
Include this small numbered section, in this order, without expanding it into a long rules list:
1. Arrive ten minutes early.
2. Choose about 3 km or about 6 km.
3. Check the notice channel for a same-day change.

Martin, another volunteer, said, “we're not trying to make every run an event; we just want it to be easy to join in.” This may appear near the end, but do not describe Martin as the club’s official spokesperson. The audience is volunteers working on site that morning. Use a plain, welcoming tone. This should be a practical day-of briefing, not a public race announcement or a full operations manual. Distinguish confirmed arrangements from estimates and unresolved details; do not fill gaps with invented people, policies, equipment, contact information, services, or decisions.

## Event overview
- **Event:** Running club spring 5K
- **Date and location:** Saturday, May 18, at Riverbend Park. The year is not supplied.
- **Start:** 9:00 a.m.; volunteer check-in begins at 7:30 a.m.
- **Expected attendance:** About 140 runners is an estimate, not a registration total. Families and a few spectators are also expected.
- The parks department permit is approved and lists the picnic shelter as the meeting point. It does not grant exclusive use of the path.

## 1. Arrival and check-in
Volunteers should check in with Mara Chen at the picnic shelter by 7:30 a.m. and collect a paper course map and a bright yellow vest. The club has 12 vests total; the notes do not say whether any remain beyond those needed by assigned volunteers, so do not promise a vest to an unconfirmed volunteer.

The park’s public restrooms are on the north side of the picnic shelter. Runners may leave bags under the shelter at their own risk. The club is not providing bag storage or supervision, and the restrooms are not reserved for the event.

## 2. Schedule
- **7:30 a.m.:** Volunteer check-in; course and station setup begins.
- **7:30–8:30 a.m.:** Course and station setup.
- **8:35 a.m.:** Planned volunteer huddle at the picnic shelter.
- **8:50 a.m.:** Runners gather.
- **9:00 a.m.:** Start.

The notes do not give an expected finish time, course closing time, or teardown deadline. Do not add one. Direct finishers toward the shelter area, but do not promise medals, food, or an awards ceremony.

## 3. Assigned jobs and open assignments
- **Mara Chen:** Volunteer lead; checks in volunteers at the picnic shelter.
- **Dev Patel:** Start and finish area; has the megaphone and plans to use it for the welcome and start instructions. There is no separate sound system.
- **Jo Reyes:** East footbridge crossing.
- **Ellis Ward and Nora King:** Water station; bringing cups and two refill jugs.
- **Tom Alvarez:** Bringing the first-aid kit. Tom is not a medical professional; do not describe him as one or imply he can provide medical care.
- **Open:** Two course marshals are still needed, one at each route-arrow location. No names have been assigned.
- **Open:** No cleanup lead has been confirmed. Do not imply cleanup is covered.

## 4. Route and water station
The measured 5K is two clockwise laps of the park’s paved 2.5K loop. Runners start by the picnic shelter and finish beside it. At the east footbridge, runners pass the playground entrance; Jo is assigned to direct them there. The path remains open to park users. Volunteers should guide runners without stopping walkers or cyclists or suggesting the club has exclusive use.

The water table is near the halfway point by the oak grove, on the inside edge of the path. Runners may take water there on either lap. Route arrows are planned at the fork near the community garden and at the west parking entrance; the two marshal assignments remain open. The parks department has not confirmed whether it will put up a temporary sign at the road entrance, so that status is unresolved.

One volunteer asked, “what if the water runs out before the second lap?” The notes do not name a refill backup or anyone to fetch water. Flag this as an unresolved practical question, not as a solved procedure.

## 5. Safety, communication, and weather
If someone is injured or needs urgent help, volunteers should call 911 first, then tell Mara as soon as practical. For a runner who seems unwell but does not appear to need urgent help, alert Mara and stay nearby if it is safe to do so. Do not provide medical advice or suggest that Tom can provide care.

If a runner goes off course, point them back toward the marked route without sending them across traffic. If the route is unclear, contact Mara rather than creating a detour. Be courteous to other park users. No walkie-talkies are listed, and Mara’s phone number is not supplied; do not invent contact details or promise radio communication.
